reason: Core equivalence is a theorem: |G| odd => 1/|G| in F_2, R=(1/|G|)sum g is an F_2-linear projector onto B^G; if span(generators) is G-stable then W_c is G-stable, R(W_c)=W_c cap B^G, and 1 in B^G, so 1 in W_c iff 1 in R(W_c). No counterexample possible under the stability hypothesis; it fails only if the generator span is not G-stable (e.g. per-block different bases, or barrel selectors not permuted consistently). Not a generic-group algorithm; plain linear algebra over F_2, nongenericity N/A (constant-factor enabler, B*D^2 unchanged). Weak points: (1) prototype reduces only columns (n=11,l=4: rows 3289 both; cols 4017->1349 = 0.336; rank 3281->1125 = 0.343), so memory saving shown is 1/|G| not 1/|G|^2; rows must be R(m*f) over orbit reps of (m,f) pairs to get the claimed /|G|^2. (2) fixed-point monomials make orbit count > N/|G| slightly. (3) Barrel C_n arm adds n selectors and a degree; net saving unmeasured, may be negative. (4) Prior art: Faugere-Svartz/Steidel isotypic decomposition already implies trivial block suffices for 1-membership; novelty low.
fix: Restate: for G-stable generator spans with |G| odd, refutation degree c* is computed exactly in the trivial isotypic block; implement row orbit reduction (rows = R(m f) over pair-orbit reps) to reach ~1/|G|^2 memory; restrict claimed benefit to Z/3 unchained arm until barrel arm measured; check G-stability of the generator span explicitly per instance.
